decision: dropped the first paper and asked for papers that fit an 8 GB budget instead
why: the first paper was ruled out for safety reasons, so it is never revisited

decision: capped every run at 8 GB of GPU memory on the one RTX 5090, models under 8B
why: results should hold for someone with an RTX 5060, not only a 5090 owner

decision: chose s1: Simple test-time scaling (arXiv 2501.19393) as the paper to replicate, Tier 1 first
why: authors used a 32B model, close to the 30B to under-8B goal, and s1K is only 1000 examples

decision: build in order: paper intake, then Tier 1 replication, then dashboard, then skill tree
why: the replication spec needs verified numbers from the paper before any training code

decision: catalog every reference, read only the ones Tier 1 depends on in full
why: a full map of the field without spending the run reading background citations

decision: fetch order: arXiv, then OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar open copy, then direct download, then a new Chrome tab, then a local fetch page
why: most blocked downloads resolve in Chrome, and the user drops in the rest without the agents waiting; closed papers are left alone

decision: run the intake as parallel subagents on the parent model, driven by pstack skills, with the orchestrator as the only decision-log writer
why: workers keep raw sources out of the orchestrator context, and one writer keeps the log consistent

why: the user asked for /to-spec, and asked for a browser seam on top of the merged event stream
